category_title: Gifted student with impulse control disorder and depression exhibiting perfectionism and anger fits
minimal_context: The student is working on a mind-games paper with varying levels of difficulty in a classroom setting right before lunch.
dialogue:
TUTOR: The application time is over. Please pass your mind-games working papers to the front so we can get ready for lunch.

STUDENT: (Holding onto the paper) I am not returning it. I have to answer all of the questions.

TUTOR: Just hand in what you have finished so far.

STUDENT: No! I will solve all the questions. I am not ending the activity without completing all of them.

TUTOR: It is time for lunch now, you need to give me the paper.

STUDENT: (Starts crying loudly) I will not return my paper unless I solve all the questions! I cannot do it but I will!

options.A: Implement systematic instruction for the mind-games paper and provide frequent, effective, and efficient feedback, either praise or corrective.
options.B: Clarify misconceptions or errors in procedural steps on the mind-games paper and re-teach the necessary skills for the activity.
options.C: Allow the student to keep the mind-games paper under the condition that he does not show it to peers, and break for lunch.
options.D: Introduce new strategies for completing the mind-games paper through modeling their use by thinking aloud during the session.
